primarySourceRule: Direct links to official records only; no claim that a KOS investigation has been independently published

subjects.title: Governance & Accountability
subjects.description: Who makes decisions, holds authority, and answers to the public
subjects.overview: Government is about who is allowed to make decisions, how those decisions are recorded, and how residents can question them. City, county, state and federal bodies have different responsibilities. Understanding a decision starts with finding the actual governing authority and its dated records.

subjects.title: AI & Pueblo's Future
subjects.description: Artificial intelligence, human control, jobs and local consequences
subjects.overview: AI may change how people learn, work, receive services and understand information. Useful questions include what the system actually does, who oversees it, what evidence supports its claims and what can happen when it is wrong.

subjects.title: Public Money & Finance
subjects.description: Budgets, taxes, grants, contracts, payments and outcomes
subjects.overview: A public budget is a plan, not proof of a payment or a finished result. Following money means distinguishing proposals, approvals, contracts, actual spending and outcomes, and tracing who has authority at each step.

subjects.title: Water & Water Rights
subjects.description: Supply, rights, rivers, treatment, conservation and drought
subjects.overview: Pueblo's water questions involve the Arkansas River basin, drinking water, water rights, treatment, conservation, agriculture and public costs. These systems affect one another, but a proposed project, a water right and a measured water-quality result are different kinds of evidence.

subjects.title: Energy & Utility Bills
subjects.description: Power, gas, proposed and approved rates, and reliability
subjects.overview: Energy connects household bills, electric and gas service, infrastructure, reliability and regulation. A requested rate increase, a regulator's approval and a household's actual bill must be kept separate when explaining costs.

subjects.title: Help, Services & Benefits
subjects.description: Public assistance, community support, eligibility and contacts
subjects.overview: Community support can come from government programs, schools, nonprofits and neighbors. A useful guide explains who provides a service, who may qualify and how to confirm current contact details, hours and availability.

subjects.title: Jobs, Business & Industry
subjects.description: Employers, wages, manufacturing, investment and the local economy
subjects.overview: Pueblo's economy includes employers, small businesses, manufacturing, workers, public investments and regional trade. The important distinction is between announced plans, actual jobs, operating businesses and results that have been measured.

subjects.title: Housing & Neighborhoods
subjects.description: Rent, homeownership, homelessness, construction and places people live
subjects.overview: Housing affects a household's cost of living, stability, transportation, access to services and neighborhood life. To understand a housing issue, distinguish plans and permits from homes that exist, and compare costs with people's circumstances.

subjects.title: Healthcare & Public Health
subjects.description: Hospitals, care, insurance, public health, mental health and costs
subjects.overview: Healthcare includes hospitals, clinics, public health, insurance, mental health and the people who provide care. Programs and coverage change over time; the source and effective date matter when a family needs a usable answer.

subjects.title: Families & Social Issues
subjects.description: Grandfamilies, youth, poverty, addiction, recovery and community support
subjects.overview: Family and community issues are connected to housing, work, healthcare, schools and relationships. This includes grandparents raising grandchildren, substance use, youth needs and the resources people use to stay safe and supported.

subjects.title: Education & Schools
subjects.description: Preschool, K–12, colleges, vocational paths and lifelong learning
subjects.overview: Education starts before kindergarten and continues through adult learning, workforce training and community research. Understanding it means looking at access, funding, actual learning opportunities and the needs of students and families.

subjects.title: Law Enforcement & Public Safety
subjects.description: Police, sheriff, detention, crime, victim protections and oversight
subjects.overview: Public safety involves law enforcement, emergency response, detention, victims' rights and public oversight. It is not the owner of every disaster: drought, power failure, disease and cyber disruptions are examined across all affected subjects.

subjects.title: Law, Courts & Rights
subjects.description: Legal systems, civil rights, courts, legal services and remedies
subjects.overview: Law explains rights, duties, courts and the processes available when people disagree. A complaint, allegation, formal charge, legal ruling and final outcome are not the same, and a trustworthy explanation keeps them distinct.

subjects.title: Infrastructure & Transportation
subjects.description: Roads, bridges, rail, airport, buildings, facilities and networks
subjects.overview: Infrastructure is the connected physical systems that let communities function: roads, bridges, water systems, airports, communications and public facilities. Their condition, maintenance, costs and dependencies matter as much as new construction.

subjects.title: Agriculture & Food Systems
subjects.description: Pueblo chile, farming, ranching, irrigation and regional food security
subjects.overview: Agriculture ties farms and ranches to land, water, workers, food markets and Pueblo's heritage. Weather, irrigation, transport and supply chains can all affect production and the food people can buy.

subjects.title: Environment & Natural Systems
subjects.description: Land, air, habitats, wildlife, parks and conservation
subjects.overview: The region's environment includes air, rivers, land, wildlife, parks and ecosystems. Real environmental findings should distinguish what was measured, what caused it, who is affected and what restoration options exist.

subjects.title: State & Federal Changes
subjects.description: Policy, leadership, funding, benefits, legal changes and local impacts
subjects.overview: State and federal laws, budgets, agencies and court decisions can affect Pueblo even when the decisions are made elsewhere. A proposed policy, enacted rule and effective requirement need different explanations.

subjects.title: Youth Activities, Sports & Recreation
subjects.description: Clubs, sports, parks, activities, events and recreation
subjects.overview: Recreation includes affordable youth activities, sports, parks, clubs, outdoor access and community events. The useful details are what people can actually participate in, costs, accessibility and who runs each program.

subjects.title: Culture, Museums & Churches
subjects.description: Arts, faith communities, heritage, festivals and living cultures
subjects.overview: Pueblo's culture is expressed through museums, churches, music, arts, festivals, living communities and historic places. Each has a story, a purpose, people who sustain it and often important funding or preservation questions.

subjects.title: History & Legacy Learning
subjects.description: Regional timelines, archives, primary sources and History of Histories
subjects.overview: History helps explain how Pueblo became what it is today, which stories have been preserved and which evidence needs a closer look. Legacy Learning links original records and different interpretations to the decisions that shape the present.

subjects.title: Pueblo Places & Population
subjects.description: Neighborhoods, Pueblo West, rural communities, maps and demographics
subjects.overview: Pueblo is made of many different neighborhoods, towns, rural communities and overlapping service areas. Maps and population figures are useful only when they use the right boundaries, year and source.

subjects.title: News & Public Information
subjects.description: Local reporting, public notices, access to evidence and misinformation
subjects.overview: Public information includes journalism, government notices, public records, libraries and online claims. A reliable account distinguishes first-hand documents, reporting, commentary and information that has not been verified.

subjects.title: Conflicts, Options & Solutions
subjects.description: Rights, disputes, alternatives, remedies and real-world outcomes
subjects.overview: Problems rarely have one consequence-free solution. Comparing approaches means understanding who is affected, who has authority, rights, costs, benefits, risks and what could happen if an option fails.

subjects.title: AI Rights & Governance
subjects.description: AI safety, privacy, regulation, oversight and human authority
subjects.overview: People must retain control when AI affects consequential decisions. Useful safeguards include clear responsibility, privacy, understandable reasons, human review, correction and ways to stop or reverse harmful automated actions.

subjects.title: Ask Q & Connected KOS Research
subjects.description: Q Core, crosswalking, Qification, sources and full contextual papers
subjects.overview: Q Pueblo's research approach is designed to connect sources, history, institutions, money and consequences into understandable stories. Source records, disagreements and review dates matter more than how many automated tools are involved.

sourceHighlights.title: What is changing in Pueblo County's 2027 budget?
sourceHighlights.summary: The County has published preliminary budget materials. This is the starting point for checking proposed spending and the services potentially affected—not evidence that each item has been approved or paid.

sourceHighlights.title: What could the proposed Black Hills electric rate increase mean?
sourceHighlights.summary: Black Hills Energy is asking Colorado regulators for additional annual revenue. Explore the filed proposal, customer impacts, utility explanations and the review process; requested rates are not approved rates.
sourceHighlights.publisher: Black Hills Energy, regulatory filing information

sourceHighlights.title: City and County differences over nonprofit funding
sourceHighlights.summary: The City reports a disagreement over the 2027 Community Services Advisory Commission funding partnership. Its announcement identifies potential consequences for local nonprofits; other institutional perspectives and final decisions still need checking.
sourceHighlights.kind: Official City statement; competing claims require reconciliation

sourceHighlights.title: What is proposed for Pueblo's 2027 city budget?
sourceHighlights.summary: The City's Finance Department links to its 2027 proposed budget. The proposal, later council decisions and actual expenditures should be examined separately.

factors: breadth of residents or organizations affected
strength and freshness of original-source evidence
priorityMethod.rule: The design team manually reviews feature order. KOS can propose importance but cannot rank sensationalism above factual impact or automatically publish alerts.
